name: Pashto (Standard Afghan)
notes: Pashto (پښتو) — Standard Afghan Pashto on a Kandahari (Southwestern) base. Eastern Iranian, ~50–60 million speakers, one of the two official languages of Afghanistan. DEFINING FEATURES vs. Persian: (1) retroflex consonants ʈ ɖ ɳ ɻ ʂ ʐ; (2) the Pashto shift Proto-Iranian *č → ts, *ǰ → dz; (3) no pharyngeals; (4) a seven-vowel system /i e ə a ɑ o u/ that contrasts by QUALITY, not length — no length mark belongs on a Pashto phoneme (Tegey & Robson 1996; Penzl 1955; David 2014). DIALECT TARGET: the Southwestern (Kandahari) values ښ = ʂ and ږ = ʐ. The same two letters read x/ɡ in Northeastern (Yusufzai) and ç/ʝ or ɕ/ʑ in the Central (Karlani) group; a spec emits one dialect, so the other readings are a documented mismatch rather than an error. ORTHOGRAPHY: the abjad leaves short vowels unwritten, and three letters are positional. Word-initial alef is a vowel carrier defaulting to a short vowel (a, i, or u), with ɑ kept only as a low-priority fallback in that same slot; آ is the letter dedicated to spelling initial /ɑ/. ⟨او⟩ opens a word on the rounded vowel Waw supplies, not on /ɑw/; word-final ه spells the final vowel (the feminine -a, or ə), not /h/. Waw and the Ye letters are matres lectionis after a consonant and glides beside a vowel. ر is the alveolar trill /r/ with the tap [ɾ] as its positional variant; that choice follows the gold's notation convention (356 r vs 1 ɾ), not a positional claim. ړ has the retroflex flap [ɽ] as its general value, with a lateral flap syllable-initially and [ɻ] elsewhere; this spec keeps ɻ because the gold's notation splits near-evenly across variants (ɽ 38, ɻ 39, ɺ̢ 11, ɺ 9 tokens) and treats that as a documented refusal to pick a positional rule rather than a positional assertion. /n/ is velar [ŋ] before a velar stop. ADSTRATE EFFECT ON DARI: some retroflex-influenced articulation in Afghan Persian speakers with Pashto contact. The unwritten short vowels remain the dominant residual error: a spelling with no vowel letter cannot be given its /ə/ or /a/ from the orthography alone, and no positional rule in this spec places one.

allophone_rules.notes: Nasal place assimilation: /n/ is velar [ŋ] before a velar stop. Standard for Pashto (Tegey & Robson 1996; David 2014).
